hypothesis: A genuinely new graph/symmetry route is to enforce continuity at the simplicial level. If continuity and unit-triangle compatibility force the m-subdivision of Delta(1) to propagate row by row as a rigid lattice triangle, then the whole continuity-preserving simplicial origami family reduces to packing k rigid side-m lattice triangles inside the side-n target triangle with n = ceil(m sqrt(k)). If that reduced graph packing already caps below 10 copies for k=10, then continuity-preserving simplicial origami is not a viable solution family.
paper_readiness_reason: This attempt gives strong exact negative evidence for a qualitatively new family. It implemented a reproducible graph-based rigidity reduction and exact compatibility-clique searches that rule out 10 rigid side-m triangles for k=10 through m=11. But it is still a family obstruction rather than a constructive smooth Hamiltonian solution, and there is no proof yet for all m.
worked: Implemented src/graph_rigid_triangle_packing.py, a new graph/symmetry-based analysis tool for continuous simplicial origami. The script verifies that once the first unit triangle seed is fixed, every later row is forced; across all 12 admissible unit-triangle seeds and for all m <= 20 tested, the propagated embedding stayed affine and vertex-injective, so every continuity-preserving simplicial unit-triangle embedding is just a rigid lattice triangle. The same script then enumerated all rigid side-m lattice-triangle placements inside the side-n target triangle with n = ceil(m sqrt(10)) and searched the compatibility graph for packings. Exact searches showed k=10 is feasible for m=1 and m=2, but for m=3 through m=11 the exact maximum is only 9 placements. Saved exact and mixed sweep artifacts under results/research_loop/.
did_not_work: The continuity-preserving simplicial origami family failed as a route to near-full density. The hoped-for fold freedom disappears: row propagation is rigid, so a single ball never becomes a new folded polyiamond, only a translated/rotated rigid side-m triangle. The reduced packing problem also fails at the target density: exact searches show that 10 rigid side-m triangles do not fit into side ceil(m sqrt(10)) for m=3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11, even though the pure area ratio there ranges from 0.9 up to about 0.9878. For example, at the attempt_007 near-full scale m=6, n=19, the perfect ratio would be 0.997229916897507, but the exact graph search finds a hard cap of 9 triangles and ratio only 0.8975069252077562.
next_step: Leave the continuity-preserving simplicial/unit-triangle origami class. The next family should be non-simplicial and break the rigid row-propagation invariant, for example via a smooth multi-chart shear or generating-function construction where a single ball image is not forced to remain a rigid lattice triangle.
patterns_noticed: Several concrete patterns emerged. First, the local rigidity is absolute in the tested model: for all 12 admissible seed unit triangles and all m <= 20 in the saved rigidity audit, the propagated rows matched the affine formula exactly and all vertices stayed distinct. That means continuity plus unit-triangle compatibility leaves no internal fold choices at all. Second, the reduced rigid-packing problem has a sharp small-m threshold for k=10: m=1 and m=2 can realize all 10 target copies exactly, with ratios 0.625 and 0.8163265306122449 respectively, but m=3 through m=11 all cap at 9 copies in the exact searches. Third, the achievable rigid-triangle ratio then oscillates with the arithmetic of n = ceil(m sqrt(10)): it is 0.81 at m=3, rises to 0.8975069252077562 at m=6, drops again to 0.833648393194707 at m=7, and climbs back to 0.8889795918367347 at m=11, tracking the same rational-approximation oscillation already seen in attempt_007. Fourth, the gap between area-only perfection and exact graph feasibility can stay large even when the area ratio is near 1: at m=10 the perfect count would give ratio 0.9765625, but the exact maximum remains 9 and ratio 0.87890625. Fifth, the placement count of rigid side-m triangles grows only moderately, from 31 at m=2 to 430 at m=11, which made exact clique search feasible farther than expected and suggests the obstruction is structural rather than a search artifact. Finally, the new family closes the specific loophole left by attempt_007: connectedness and continuity are not enough if the continuous image class itself is rigid and its exact packing graph still caps at 9.
